reviews.text: Ether.fi is a liquid staking protocol on Ethereum, allowing users to stake ETH and receive liquid tokens for DeFi use. Launched in 2023, it has grown with restaking features. In 2025, it's integrated with major chains and offers high yields. The team is transparent, but security audits are key. It’s useful for yield farmers.

Ether.fi is a decentralized, non-costudal staking and restaking protocol running on the Ethereum network.  eETH, the token given in exchange for staked ETH, provides liquidity to the user and can be used in DEFI protocols. eETH may have increasing value, but you can also use it for defi by converting it to weth. ethfi is the governance and incentive token of ether.fi. It has a total supply of 1 billion, and 60.9 percent of the supply is in circulation.

Ether.fi is a liquid staking protocol enabling users to earn Ethereum staking rewards while maintaining liquidity through eETH token. Unlike centralized staking, it’s non-custodial: users stake ETH to mint stTokens (e.g. eETH) without handing over keys. Ether.fi goes further by restaking those assets on EigenLayer for extra yield. This dual-layer staking earns yields up to around 11% (triple that of standard ETH staking). However, restaking adds risks and there’s a 7-day unlock delay. The protocol operates with distributed validator network ensuring decentralization

Ether.fi is a non custodial decentralized finance platform that focuses on staking, restaking, liquid vaults and crypto physical cards. The platform was built on Ethereum and has a very large total value locked which indicates users confidence and satisfaction with the platform. Ether.fi was founded by highly experienced team members with backing of top tier VCs like Consensys and OKX Ventures in addition. to strong partnerships with prominent web 3 projects like Eigen layer and Plasma.  They have a very active social media community and strong security measures which is reflected in their multiple up to date third party audits and active bug bounty program.

Ether.fi strikes me as an interesting “stake to earn” platform it’s like a game for validators with stable yields. I find its model innovative, and it’s impressive it has $3 billion of ETH in its pool with backing from big funds. On the other hand, its doxxing rule needing to reveal identity if staking <2 ETH feels odd and a bit off putting.

Ether.fi is basically one of the more interesting liquid staking platforms right now. What makes it stand out is that it gives users a non custodial way to stake ETH meaning you stay in control of your keys while still earning staking rewards.
The ecosystem around it (like eETH and the restaking angle) has been getting a lot of attention, especially with the whole EigenLayer hype. The team looks active, and the project keeps shipping new features.
The only downside is that restaking is still a risky and experimental area, and the space is getting crowded with competitors. But overall, Ether.fi feels like a solid project with real traction.
